name: Helsingin perhehoito (City of Helsinki family care: becoming a foster parent)
coverage: City of Helsinki (the city runs its own child welfare; foster families may live up to 250 km from Helsinki)
notes: The page names two family care workers to contact by phone or email. Single people, single parents, couples and same-sex couples can foster if life is stable. A carer may work, but one parent is expected to stay at home for a while when a child arrives. Free preparation of about six months, in several groups a year or family by family. It lists 2026 fees: a care fee of EUR 1,637.23 a month for a child aged 0 to 11 with a carer at home and EUR 1,927.16 for ages 12 to 17. A downloadable PDF application form (Hakemus perhekodiksi tai -hoitajaksi) is linked. Page updated 17 September 2026; the English page says the same.

name: Helsingin kaupungin adoptioneuvonta (City of Helsinki adoption counselling)
coverage: Residents of Helsinki, Vantaa and Kerava (per the page)
notes: Adoption starts with adoption counselling, which is free and covers domestic, intercountry and step-parent adoption. People register by contacting one of the counselling social workers, who send a registration form. The page names four social workers. Kela's adoption allowance page still lists the City of Helsinki as an intercountry adoption service provider; a 2020 city decision seen in search results says it had taken no new intercountry clients since 2015 (unverified). The city's adoption page (updated 20 August 2025) still places the Adoption Board at Valvira; since 2026 it sits in the Licensing and Supervisory Agency.

name: Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialue (Vantaa and Kerava wellbeing services county): Ryhdy sijaisperheeksi
coverage: Vantaa and Kerava wellbeing services county (VAKE)
notes: A short application form (Webropol) commits to nothing; staff then get in touch. It asks for three things: you can commit to a child for a long time, your life is stable and safe, and your home has room for a child. Single people and same-sex couples are welcome. Preparation is PRIDE. A county news item of 10 September 2026 says the care fee for a carer at home can be over EUR 1,900 a month, plus expenses. Form fields not read.

name: Perhehoitokeskus Pihlaja (Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue, Central Uusimaa wellbeing services county family care centre)
coverage: Central Uusimaa wellbeing services county (Keusote)
stated_response_time: A social worker gets in touch within a month of the application (viimeistään kuukauden kuluessa hakemuksesta)
notes: People apply in the OmaKeusote online service, which needs strong electronic identification. Pihlaja recruits, prepares, assesses and trains carers. Applicants for preparation must be at least 25. A couple should have been together about five years and lived together about two; the family's youngest child should be at least 2. The child needs a room of their own with a window by school age. Free preparation. Checks include a doctor's certificate, a criminal record extract, and social services and police records when a child is about to be placed.

name: Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (Western Uusimaa wellbeing services county): Perhehoito lastensuojelussa
coverage: Western Uusimaa wellbeing services county (LUVN; preparation groups in Karjaa, Espoo and Lohja)
notes: The pages list three family care coordinators with phone and email, and a family care phone line on weekdays. Contact commits to nothing. For PRIDE, the county sends an application after first contact, then makes a home visit. Groups ran or were planned in Karjaa (autumn 2026), Espoo (October 2026 to February 2027) and Lohja (February to May 2027), with Teams information sessions on 4 November and 2 December. Some pages are drawn by script and were read in a headless browser. Its 2026 fee sheet lists EUR 1,737.86 a month for a child aged 0 to 11 with a full-time carer.

name: Itä-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (Eastern Uusimaa wellbeing services county): Haluatko perhehoitajaksi?
coverage: Eastern Uusimaa wellbeing services county
notes: The family care pages are written mainly for care of older and disabled people. They name a separate contact for children's family care at the Loviisa family centre. The page's online form (Microsoft Forms, although the link text says Google Forms) books a family care pre-interview; it is unclear whether it is used for foster care of children. We found no separate recruitment page for foster families.

name: Varsinais-Suomen hyvinvointialue (Varha, Southwest Finland wellbeing services county): Sijaisperheeksi lapselle tai nuorelle
coverage: Southwest Finland wellbeing services county (Varha)
notes: Becoming a foster parent starts with PRIDE preparation of about four months: an intake interview, nine three-hour group meetings, at least two family meetings and a final assessment. The page gives a shared email address and three named contacts. It lists absolute barriers, including criminal record entries, physical punishment, active child welfare or income support client status, and a partner who objects. Varha also has pages for emergency foster families and support families.

name: Satakunnan hyvinvointialue (Satakunta wellbeing services county): Lastensuojelun perhehoito
coverage: Satakunta wellbeing services county (two areas, north and south, each with its own contact)
notes: People apply online in the Sata service (asiointi.sata.fi) or on a downloadable Word form (Hakemus perhehoitajaksi, updated October 2025). The county runs PRIDE of about six months twice a year, with nine group meetings, and makes a home visit before preparation starts. One parent or both may work outside the home, depending on the child's needs, and a single person can foster.

name: Perhehoitoyksikkö Kanerva (Oma Häme, Kanta-Häme wellbeing services county family care unit)
coverage: Kanta-Häme wellbeing services county (Oma Häme)
notes: The county's robots.txt asks automated readers to stay out, so we did not read its pages. Search results show Kanerva coordinates and provides child welfare family care for the whole county, and supports, trains and prepares carers. They also show a 2026 child welfare family care guideline (PDF). We found no application route in the results.

name: Perhehoito Luotsi (Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialue, Pirkanmaa wellbeing services county): Luotsaamme sinut sijaisperheeksi
coverage: Pirkanmaa wellbeing services county (Pirha)
notes: The county's robots.txt asks automated readers to stay out, so we did not read its pages. Search results show Luotsi is the county's child welfare family care unit. It recruits and prepares foster families and keeps emergency foster families on call. A downloadable application form (Hakemus perhehoitajaksi) goes to Luotsi in Tampere by post or email. A 2026 fee table is also published.

name: Päijät-Hämeen perhehoito (Päijät-Häme wellbeing services county): Lastensuojelun perhehoito
coverage: Päijät-Häme wellbeing services county (about 150 foster families)
notes: People apply on a form in the Päijät-Sote app, after signing in with online banking codes, and then email the family care social workers, because the app does not tell them about new applications. Two social workers are named. PRIDE groups start at least twice a year (next from 20 January 2027): nine group meetings and three to five family meetings. Preparation is free, but the written materials cost EUR 55, refunded when a long-term placement starts. Read in a headless browser; page updated 30 October 2026.

name: Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialue (Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county): toimeksiantosopimussuhteinen perhehoito
coverage: Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county
notes: We found no recruitment web page; the child welfare page we read has no family care link. The county's family care guideline, in force from 1 February 2026, says interested families should contact its family care coordinators. It asks for a criminal record extract no more than six months old, checked again every three years. Pesäpuu's list shows PRIDE in Kymenlaakso twice a year, in Kotka in autumn and Kouvola in spring (under the county's old name, Kymsote).

name: Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue (South Karelia wellbeing services county): Lastensuojelun perhehoito ja sijaisperheet
coverage: South Karelia wellbeing services county (formerly Eksote)
notes: The page gives a support team phone line in office hours and two named contacts. Preparation runs once a year, is free and commits to nothing; no particular qualification is needed, and a relative can be the child's carer. An information session was held in Lappeenranta on 2 September 2026, with no need to sign up. The 2026 family care guideline is linked. Page edited 5 October 2026.

name: Etelä-Savon hyvinvointialue Eloisa (South Savo wellbeing services county): Sijaisperheeksi ryhtyminen ja perhehoidon tuki
coverage: South Savo wellbeing services county (Eloisa)
notes: An ordinary family, a childless couple or a person living alone can foster. People sign up by email by 21 December 2026 for the spring 2027 PRIDE group in Mikkeli (2 February to 19 June 2027): intake interviews in January, nine sessions, family meetings and a final assessment. Teams information sessions were held in September 2026. One social worker is named as the contact. Page edited 4 August 2026.

name: Pohjois-Savon hyvinvointialue (North Savo wellbeing services county): Lasten ja nuorten tukiperhe- ja perhehoito
coverage: North Savo wellbeing services county (19 municipalities; family care support unit in Kuopio)
notes: People contact the family care coordinators by phone or by a shared email address; the page lists phone lines by role. In PRIDE the family and the trainers assess readiness together, and both partners of a couple must take part. Carers give criminal record extracts, a doctor's statement and consent to a report from their local social services. Short-term care needs extra preparation. Read in a headless browser, because the page menu filled the plain text.

name: Pohjois-Savon hyvinvointialue (North Savo wellbeing services county): Adoptioneuvonta (adoption counselling)
coverage: North Savo wellbeing services county
notes: Free statutory counselling for domestic, intercountry and step-parent adoption. For intercountry adoption the page says to contact Pelastakaa Lapset (Save the Children Finland) directly. Step-parent adoption starts with a child maintenance officer (lastenvalvoja); phone lines are listed by area. Read in a headless browser.

name: Siun sote (North Karelia wellbeing services county): Lastensuojelun perhehoito ja sijaisperheet
coverage: North Karelia wellbeing services county (Siun sote)
notes: People apply by contacting the family care support team; contact commits to nothing. Families with children, one- or two-parent families and people living alone can apply. Every foster family has its own adviser from the team. Short-term care lasts up to three months. Search results show the county started its first own PRIDE group in February 2026 (unverified). Pelastakaa Lapset also runs family-by-family PRIDE in North Karelia.

name: Perhehoitoyksikkö Koivikko (Keski-Suomen hyvinvointialue, Central Finland wellbeing services county)
coverage: Central Finland wellbeing services county (Hyvaks)
notes: The electronic application sits behind strong electronic identification; a pre-information form is also in the OmaHyvaks app. People with a non-disclosure order for their address should contact staff instead. Carers must be at least 25, single or a couple, with an age gap to the child of no more than 45 years (more allowed for short-term care). PRIDE has nine group meetings, mostly in spring and autumn. Checks after preparation include a doctor's certificate, a criminal record extract and police records.

name: Etelä-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue (South Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county): Lastensuojelun perhehoito
coverage: South Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county
notes: The county's family care unit recruits carers all year and prepares and approves them through PRIDE. Families hear about new PRIDE groups from the family care social workers. A pre-information form (Word file, 2026) is linked from the page. The 2026 fee sheet lists a basic care fee of EUR 1,893.38 a month.

name: Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue / Österbottens välfärdsområde (Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county): Lastensuojelun perhehoito
coverage: Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county (bilingual, Finnish and Swedish)
notes: Filling in the form commits to nothing; staff then call to tell you more. You can also phone. Before PRIDE the county checks social services, police and criminal records and asks about health. PRIDE has nine group meetings, home visits and homework, and ends with a written and spoken assessment. For short-term family care at least one parent must be at home. Form fields not read. Page updated 16 September 2026.

name: Soite (Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue, Central Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county): Perhehoitajaksi lapselle tai nuorelle
coverage: Central Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county (Soite; 8 municipalities)
notes: People apply by contacting the family care workers by phone or email. A couple, a person living alone or a single parent can foster; the child needs a room or space of their own. Barriers include repeated or long-term child welfare or income support client status, a weak financial position, substance or mental health problems and a custody dispute. PRIDE lasts about six months. An English page also exists.

name: Pohde (Pohjois-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue, North Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county): Hae meille perhehoitajaksi
coverage: North Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county (Perhehoidon keskus, the family care centre in Oulu)
notes: People phone a family care social worker or send a Word application form for preparation to the family care centre. Staff get in touch once they have processed it and arrange a pre-interview. A Teams information session was held on 24 November 2026, and PRIDE groups were forming in Oulu and in Ylivieska (from January 2027). Listed barriers include financial difficulty, housing problems, substance or mental health problems, serious illness and serious crimes against children.

name: Kainuun hyvinvointialue (Kainuu wellbeing services county): Lasten ja nuorten perhehoito
coverage: Kainuu wellbeing services county (family social work in Kajaani)
notes: The child welfare page links a family care brochure (updated 5 September 2025) and a 2026 fee sheet. The brochure gives a phone line for the children's family care team in Kajaani. People who want to foster must complete PRIDE first. The care fee is taxable and builds pension; the expense payment is deductible in tax. The brochure still names the repealed Family Carers Act.

name: Lapin hyvinvointialue (Lapha, Lapland wellbeing services county): PRIDE-ennakkovalmennus
coverage: Lapland wellbeing services county
notes: The county's robots.txt asks automated readers to stay out, so we did not read its pages. A search result shows a page asking 'Are you interested in being a foster family?' about a PRIDE group from September 2026 to January 2027. We found no application route in the results.

name: Kommunernas socialtjänst (KST, Åland's joint municipal social services): Familjevård
coverage: Åland (KST runs social services for the Åland municipalities)
notes: In Swedish. Single people and cohabiting couples, with or without children, can become a family home (familjehem); there must be room for the child to have their own room. KST assesses finances and health and checks social, criminal and police records. Preparation is PRIDE: eight sessions and three to four family meetings, free, run by KST since 2023. The page says Åland still applies the Family Carers Act of 1992, not the 2015 Act. Our reader saw only part of the page, so we did not record how to get in touch.

name: Kommunernas socialtjänst (KST): Adoption (adoptionsrådgivning, adoption counselling)
coverage: Åland
notes: In Swedish. People thinking of adopting contact one of KST's child welfare officers or Pelastakaa Lapset (Rädda Barnen) directly; Åland belongs to its Southern Finland district for adoption. Counselling takes about 10 to 12 months, with meetings at its Helsinki office and home visits. KST pays for the counselling; the family pays its own travel.

name: Perhehoitoliitto ry (Finnish Family Care Association): Olisiko sinusta perhehoitajaksi?
coverage: Finland (national family care association with regional carers' associations)
notes: Information and signposting; it does not approve carers. Its pages explain how to become a foster parent, list information sessions across Finland and list the contacts of family care organisers. It coordinates the national Ajoissa kotiin recruitment campaign (autumn 2026). The page carries advertisements from public and private providers. The old address perhehoitajaksi.fi leads here.

name: Pesäpuu ry (child welfare development centre): PRIDE-valmennus
coverage: Finland (develops the PRIDE preparation used for foster and adoptive parents)
notes: Not a front door itself: it trains PRIDE trainers and publishes a list of bodies that run PRIDE regularly. Preparation is run by wellbeing services counties, regional family care units, organisations and private providers. It also has material on preparing relatives who become foster carers. Page updated 27 October 2026.

name: Ammatillisten perhekotien liitto ry (APKL, Association of Professional Family Homes)
coverage: Finland (members' association for licensed professional family homes, listed in five regions)
notes: A members' association for professional family homes (ammatillinen perhekoti), which need a permit and may care for up to seven people. Its site lists member homes by region and their free places, mainly for placing authorities, and has a contact form we did not read. We found no recruitment of new carers on the pages read; our reader saw mostly menus.

name: Pelastakaa Lapset ry (Save the Children Finland): Sijaisvanhemmaksi
coverage: Finland (regional offices in Helsinki, Turku, Tampere, Jyväskylä, Joensuu and Oulu)
notes: A charity that recruits, prepares, assesses and supports foster families for wellbeing services counties, including integrating family care for children who arrive without a guardian. Free PRIDE or family-by-family preparation. The form asks for first name, surname, street address, town, postcode, email, phone, the nearest regional office, how you heard and consent. A national Teams information session was listed for 9 December 2026.

name: Pelastakaa Lapset ry (Save the Children Finland): Adoptiotoiminta (adoption counselling)
coverage: Finland (adoption counselling in all its regional offices)
notes: Its page says it is the only private provider licensed to give adoption counselling, which is free. It stopped taking new clients for its intercountry adoption service after 31 December 2024, although Kela's page still lists it as a provider. Wellbeing services counties can buy counselling from it; North Savo and Åland send people to it.

name: Perhepalvelut Ruori Oy (SOS-Lapsikylä, SOS Children's Villages Finland): Sijaisvanhemmaksi
coverage: Finland (family care areas in the south, east, west, Pirkanmaa and Central Finland, and the north)
notes: A social enterprise wholly owned by SOS-Lapsikylä that now runs its child welfare services (company form, so the operator type may need checking). It recruits and prepares foster carers, holds information webinars and offers a free information pack. The pack request form is drawn by script and did not appear to our reader. Carers get a care fee, expenses and start-up compensation.

name: Familar Oy (Mehiläinen group): Sijaisperheeksi
coverage: Finland (regional family care units; the pages read do not list them)
notes: A private child welfare provider in the Mehiläinen group. It recruits foster and support families and prepares them with its own Famile model, which starts with preparation and continues as support during the placement. The page names one foster family coordinator to contact by phone or email. Page updated 24 March 2026.

name: Hoivatie: Etsimme sijaisperheitä (family care)
coverage: Offices in Oulu, Rovaniemi, Helsinki, Turku and Seinäjoki; it seeks families across Finland, especially Uusimaa, Turku and Tampere, including Swedish- and English-speaking families
notes: Legal form not checked. It prepares new families with PRIDE; groups were listed for Seinäjoki (December 2026 and spring 2027), Oulu and Lapland, and Southwest Finland and Satakunta (spring 2027). The contact form asks for name, home municipality, phone, email (optional), whether to be contacted by phone or email, what you would like to know and how you heard. A Teams information session was held on 5 November 2026.

name: Perhehoitokumppanit Suomessa Oy (PKS): Ryhdy sijaisperheeksi
coverage: The pages read do not say which areas it serves
notes: A private family care provider that says it has prepared and supported carers for nearly 20 years. The contact form asks for first name, surname, email, phone, home town, a short note about yourself, whether you are interested in foster care, support family work or both, and consent to its privacy notice. It also advertises on Perhehoitoliitto's page.

name: Validia: Sijaisvanhemmuus ja perhehoito
coverage: Offices in Helsinki and Tampere (the pages read do not give a wider area)
notes: Legal form not checked, so the operator type may need checking. It offers PRIDE preparation and regular support once a placement starts, and says no social or education qualification is needed. Family care advisers answer by a shared email and phone line, and named staff are listed for the Helsinki and Tampere offices. A downloadable guide to becoming a foster parent is linked.

name: Interpedia ry: kansainvälinen adoptio (intercountry adoption service)
coverage: Finland (intercountry adoption from South Africa, India, Colombia, Taiwan and Thailand; office in Helsinki)
notes: A licensed intercountry adoption service provider. The first step is adoption counselling from the wellbeing services county or Pelastakaa Lapset; people usually register with Interpedia during counselling. The information pack form asks only for an email address. Its 2026 costs page lists a registration fee of EUR 550 and service fees in three instalments. Waiting usually takes a few years. Suomi.fi links to its information package.

name: Adoptiolautakunta (Finnish Adoption Board, in the Licensing and Supervisory Agency, Lupa- ja valvontavirasto)
coverage: Finland (national permit and supervisory authority; Hague Convention central authority)
notes: lvv.fi refused our reader (HTTP 403), so this row rests on the Adoption Act and on pages that link to the Board. Since 1 January 2026 the Board sits in the Licensing and Supervisory Agency, which replaced Valvira (Adoption Act s 86, as amended). It grants adoption permits after counselling. Interpedia says applicants send the permit application on a secure electronic form, and that the Board lists adoption counselling contacts for each wellbeing services county.

name: Adoptioperheet ry (Finnish Adoptive Families association)
coverage: Finland (national peer support association)
notes: Peer support for people waiting to adopt and for adoptive families: mentors, groups, camps and online events. It does not arrange adoptions. Suomi.fi points people thinking about adoption to it. Its site has a contact form we did not read; our reader saw mostly menus on the page for people waiting to adopt.

name: Suomi.fi: Adopting a child (national public service information, Digital and Population Data Services Agency)
coverage: Finland (national information page; we read the English version)
notes: Information only. It tells people to apply for adoption counselling through their wellbeing services county's social services, and links Interpedia, Pelastakaa Lapset and Adoptioperheet. It says married couples and people living alone over 25 can adopt, the age gap may not exceed 45 years and the applicant may not be over 50. Updated 26 November 2026.
